scenario: A patient becomes acutely disturbed and the team agree that seclusion is now the only safe option.
question: Under the Trust seclusion policy, who may authorise the implementation of seclusion?
options: The nurse in charge, a psychiatrist or an approved clinician
The bleep holder or the on-call manager
Any registered nurse on shift
Only the patient's Responsible Clinician (RC)
rationale: The policy states it must be either the nurse in charge, a psychiatrist or an approved clinician that authorises seclusion, and that person must have seen the patient immediately prior to it commencing.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

question: How often must nursing reviews take place during an episode of seclusion under Trust policy?
options: At least every hour
At least twice in every 24 hours
At least every four hours
At least every two hours
rationale: The Trust policy and the seclusion timetable appendix both set nursing reviews at least every two hours, and they stay two hourly even after the first Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: Seclusion commences at 14:00 and the patient's consultant was not involved in the decision.
question: By when must the initial medical review take place under Trust policy?
options: Within the first hour of seclusion commencing
Within two hours of seclusion commencing
Within four hours of seclusion commencing
At the next scheduled ward round
rationale: Where the consultant was not involved in the decision to seclude, the policy requires a face to face initial medical review within the first hour, recorded on the SystmOne 'Seclusion Review' document.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: You have been allocated to observe a patient who has just gone into seclusion.
question: How often must the observing staff member document the patient's behaviour under Trust policy?
options: Every 5 minutes
Hourly
Every 30 minutes
A minimum of every 15 minutes
rationale: The policy requires continuous observation with a record made a minimum of every 15 minutes in the 'Seclusion Case Notes' section of SystmOne, including food and fluid intake, respiratory rate and ACVPU on the relevant charts.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

question: Who normally takes the seclusion co-ordinator role at this Trust?
options: The nurse in charge of the shift, unless the role is allocated to someone else
The patient's named nurse
The bleep holder
The ward manager, who holds the role for the whole episode
rationale: The policy says the seclusion co-ordinator would be the nurse in charge on shift unless specifically nominated to another member of staff, and the role changes on a shift by shift basis.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

question: When must the first Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review of a seclusion episode happen, and how often after that?
options: Within 12 hours, then every 12 hours
Within 48 hours, then twice weekly
As soon as possible within 24 hours, then once in every 24 hours
At the next working day ward round, then weekly
rationale: The policy says the MDT review should take place as soon as possible within 24 hours of seclusion commencing, and then once in every 24 hours.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

question: Which of these does the Trust policy state for a patient who is in seclusion?
options: They must never be deprived of their clothing and must always be able to see a clock
Clothing may be removed at the discretion of the nurse in charge
A clock is only required in designated seclusion suites
Reading material is prohibited in all cases
rationale: The policy states a patient in seclusion must never be deprived of their clothing, and that they should be able to always have sight of a clock, with access to sensory resources, radio or reading material where clinically appropriate and safe.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: Seclusion has just commenced on your ward and you are completing the paperwork.
question: What level of DATIX does the Trust policy require to be completed when a seclusion episode starts?
options: A Low DATIX
No DATIX unless there was an injury
A Major DATIX
A Moderate DATIX
rationale: Under ward level monitoring the policy states that when a seclusion episode is commenced a Moderate DATIX will be completed as soon as possible, documenting which patient has required seclusion and why. Long-term segregation, by contrast, is recorded as Major.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

question: What does the current Trust policy say about the door hatches on seclusion room doors?
options: They may be used for passing food and drink only
They may be used by two staff working together
They may be used for medication administration
They must not be used, because of their proximity to the door handle
rationale: A July 2025 amendment states door hatches must not be used due to their proximity to the door handle, and that each hatch carries a sign reading 'Warning, Hatch not in use'.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: A patient is about to be placed in seclusion and staff have safely completed a search.
question: Where must the search and any property removed be recorded under Trust policy?
options: In the Seclusion Care Pathway, with removed property logged and held in safekeeping on the ward
In the ward property book only
In a DATIX report only
On the whiteboard outside the seclusion room
rationale: The policy requires the patient to be searched before seclusion starts, recorded within the 'Seclusion Care Pathway', with any property removed logged on that document and placed in safekeeping on the ward.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: You are working through the Section 136 suite grab bag checklist at the start of your shift.
question: According to the Trust checklist, when should the oxygen cylinder be replaced?
options: If it is less than half full
Monthly, regardless of contents
Only when it is empty
If it is less than three quarters full
rationale: The Section 136 grab bag checklist instructs staff to replace the oxygen cylinder if it is less than three quarters full. The checklist is laid out with a column for each day of the week, so it is a daily check.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 136 Suite Emergency Equipment Grab Bag Checklist
sourceDate: V5, 08 April 2025

scenario: Two hours into a seclusion episode the nursing review is due. You were part of the team that took the decision to seclude.
question: What does the Trust policy require of the staff carrying out the nursing review?
options: One registered nurse, who may be anyone on shift
Two registered nurses, both independent of the ward
One registered nurse and one healthcare assistant
Two registered nurses, one of whom was not involved in the decision to seclude
rationale: The policy states the nursing review must include two registered nurses, one of whom was not involved in the decision to seclude.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: The consultant psychiatrist was present and authorised the seclusion.
question: What does the Trust policy require in this situation?
options: A separate initial medical review must still be done by a different doctor within the hour
The seclusion co-ordinator records the review on the consultant's behalf
No medical documentation is needed until the 24 hour Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review
The consultant must record their assessment as a medical review within the first hour, using the SystmOne 'Seclusion Review' document
rationale: Where the consultant was involved in the decision to seclude, their review prior to seclusion constitutes the initial medical review, but they must record it within the first hour on the 'Seclusion Review' document on SystmOne.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

question: After the initial medical review, how often are medical reviews required until the patient has their first Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review?
options: Every two hours
Twice in 24 hours
Every six hours
Every four hours
rationale: The policy requires four hourly medical reviews after the initial medical review until the first MDT review. Only after that initial MDT review do medical reviews drop to at least twice in every 24 hours.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: A patient has been in seclusion since 22:00 and the 24 hour Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review falls in the night.
question: Who must the out of hours MDT review consist of under Trust policy?
options: Two registered nurses and the seclusion co-ordinator
The bleep holder alone
A nursing member of the leadership team or the bleep holder, and the on-call consultant or nominated deputy
The ward manager and the patient's Responsible Clinician (RC)
rationale: Out of hours the policy requires the MDT review to consist of a nursing member of the leadership team, or the bleep holder, together with the on-call consultant or their nominated deputy.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: No designated seclusion room is available, so a patient meeting the criteria for seclusion is secluded in a quiet room.
question: Who must be notified under Trust policy?
options: The Matron, the Area Service Manager and the Head of Nursing
The bleep holder only
The Care Quality Commission within 24 hours
The Executive Director of Nursing only
rationale: For seclusion outside a designated seclusion room, the policy requires the Matron, Area Service Manager and Head of Nursing to be notified, the use of a non-designated room to be clearly documented on the DATIX, and the full seclusion pathway to be followed.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: At a two hourly nursing review the patient is calm and settled and the nurses feel seclusion could safely end.
question: Can that nursing review end the seclusion under Trust policy?
options: No, only a Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) or independent review can end seclusion
Yes, but only if the patient has been secluded for less than four hours
Yes, following a discussion with the Responsible Clinician (RC) or duty doctor, in person or by telephone
No, nursing reviews can only recommend a reduction in restrictions
rationale: The policy lists a nurses review as one of the four routes to ending seclusion, provided there has been a discussion with the Responsible Clinician or duty doctor, which can be in person or on the telephone.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: As part of a graded plan, the seclusion door is opened for a planned period so the patient can use the secure courtyard.
question: What does the Trust policy say about this?
options: It ends the seclusion episode and a new episode must be opened on return
It does not constitute an end to seclusion
It converts the episode to long-term segregation
It pauses the review clock until the patient returns
rationale: The policy notes explicitly that opening the door for planned periods, for example access to the secure courtyard, does not constitute an end to seclusion. This kind of flexibility is described as a way of evaluating the patient under less restriction without terminating the episode.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: The ward is short staffed and a student nurse on placement offers to sit on the seclusion observation.
question: How does the Trust policy define who can carry out seclusion observations?
options: Any member of the nursing team, including students under supervision
Registered nurses only

A suitably skilled professional who has completed the observation skills booklet and is compliant on the Electronic Staff Record (ESR); student nurses and student Allied Health Professionals cannot do it
Any staff member who has completed Positive and Safe training
rationale: The policy defines a suitably skilled professional as someone who has completed the observation skills booklet and is compliant on ESR, and states that student nurses and student AHPs cannot undertake observations.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: A four hourly medical review was missed overnight because no doctor was available.
question: What does the Trust policy require when a seclusion review is not completed as set out in the process?
options: Nothing, provided the next review happens on time
The rationale must be documented in the Electronic Patient Record (EPR) and a DATIX completed
The seclusion episode must be ended immediately
The seclusion co-ordinator must inform the Care Quality Commission
rationale: The policy states at the start of the review section that if any reviews are not completed as per the process, the rationale must be documented in EPR and a DATIX completed. It also requires a DATIX by the seclusion co-ordinator if a doctor does not arrive for the initial medical review.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: A Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) is considering whether a patient with a sustained risk of harm to others should be placed on long-term segregation (LTS).
question: What does the Trust policy say about providing LTS at this Trust?
options: Every inpatient unit has an LTS suite available
LTS can be started by the ward Multidisciplinary Team alone if the risk is sustained

The Trust does not have the clinical environment for LTS, so it may only be considered in extenuating circumstances and only after written confirmation from the Director of Nursing, AHPs and Patient Experience
LTS is prohibited outright at this Trust with no exceptions
rationale: The policy states DHCFT does not have the clinical environment necessary to care for people in LTS, that it should only be considered in extenuating circumstances, and that it can only be instigated following written confirmation from the Director of Nursing, AHPs and Patient Experience.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: Long-term segregation (LTS) has just been agreed for a patient.
question: Who is responsible for the LTS care plan and within what timeframe must it be completed?
options: The Responsible Clinician (RC), within 72 hours
The ward manager, within 24 hours of LTS commencing
The named nurse, by the end of the first week
The Head of Nursing, within 48 hours
rationale: The policy makes the ward manager responsible for ensuring an LTS care plan is completed within 24 hours of LTS commencing, focused on what needs to be achieved for LTS to be terminated.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: An informal patient becomes acutely disturbed and, as a last resort, has to be secluded to prevent harm to others.
question: What does the Trust policy require in this situation?
options: An assessment for an emergency application for detention under the Mental Health Act must be undertaken immediately
Seclusion can continue as normal because the patient consented to go into the room
The patient must be discharged from the ward
The seclusion pathway does not apply to informal patients
rationale: The policy states that if seclusion becomes necessary for an informal patient as a last resort, an assessment for an emergency application for detention under the Act should be undertaken immediately. The full seclusion pathway and safeguards still apply.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

question: Under the Trust's seclusion monitoring arrangements, who is responsible for ensuring the seclusion suite is fit for use daily?
options: The ward manager
The bleep holder
The Positive and Safe team
The estates department
rationale: The ward level monitoring section states that the bleep holder will ensure the seclusion suite is fit for use daily, and that the suite is checked a minimum of once per day and cleaned and made ready as soon as possible after an episode ends.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: The eight hour independent review is being arranged.
question: Who must make up the independent Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review under Trust policy?
options: Any three members of the ward team not on duty at the time of the incident
The Responsible Clinician (RC), the ward manager and the seclusion co-ordinator
A Matron, a Head of Nursing and a commissioner representative

An approved clinician or consultant psychiatrist (or nominated deputy), a nurse, and an Independent Mental Health Advocate (IMHA) where the patient has one, none of whom were involved in the decision to seclude
rationale: The policy specifies the independent review membership as an approved clinician or consultant psychiatrist (or nominated deputy), a nurse, and an IMHA in cases where the patient has one, all of whom must not have been involved in the initial decision to seclude.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: A seclusion episode has now run beyond seven days.
question: What does Trust policy require for prolonged seclusion of over seven days?
options: A risk strategy meeting organised by the Responsible Clinician (RC) or nominated deputy, followed by a weekly independent Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review
Automatic conversion to long-term segregation
A referral to the Care Quality Commission
Daily independent reviews until seclusion ends
rationale: The policy states that in the event of prolonged seclusion over 7 days a risk strategy meeting should be organised by the RC or their nominated deputy, after which an independent MDT reviews the patient once a week to identify ways to reduce restrictions or end seclusion.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: It is 03:00, a four hourly medical review is due and the patient is asleep. The doctor and seclusion co-ordinator agree it would not be appropriate to wake them.
question: The policy allows the doctor's attendance to be replaced by a telephone call with the seclusion co-ordinator. What limit does it place on this?
options: It can only be used once during the whole episode
No more than two consecutive four hourly medical reviews may be undertaken in this way
It can be used for any review overnight without limit
It is only permitted at weekends and on bank holidays
rationale: The policy permits a telephone call with the seclusion co-ordinator to replace the doctor's attendance for a night time four hourly medical review when the patient is asleep, recorded on the SystmOne 'Seclusion Review' document, but no more than two consecutive reviews may be done this way.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: A patient is being managed under the long-term segregation (LTS) pathway.
question: Which set of reviews matches the Trust policy for LTS?
options: Two hourly nursing reviews, four hourly medical reviews and a weekly Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review

Hourly documentation by observing staff, an approved clinician review every 24 hours, a weekly MDT review including an Independent Mental Health Advocate (IMHA) or Independent Mental Capacity Advocate (IMCA) if the patient has one, and four weekly reviews by a professional not involved with the case
Daily approved clinician review and a monthly MDT review only
15 minute observation records and a fortnightly independent review
rationale: The LTS section sets out hourly documentation of the patient's condition by observing staff, physical health monitoring as per care plan, an approved clinician review every 24 hours, a weekly MDT review including an IMHA or IMCA if the patient has one, and four weekly reviews by a professional not involved with the case.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: Long-term segregation (LTS) for a patient has now continued for more than three months.
question: What additional review does Trust policy require, and who arranges it?
options: A Care Quality Commission inspection, arranged by the Trust board
An extra internal Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review, arranged by the Responsible Clinician (RC)

External three monthly reviews arranged by the ward manager, including a professional from outside the Trust, an Independent Mental Health Advocate (IMHA) where possible and a commissioner where appropriate
A second opinion appointed doctor visit, arranged by the Mental Health Act office
rationale: Where LTS continues for more than 3 months the policy requires external three monthly reviews to be arranged by the ward manager, including a professional from outside the Trust, an IMHA where possible and a commissioner where appropriate.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

question: How must long-term segregation (LTS) be recorded on DATIX under Trust policy?
options: As a Moderate incident, the same as seclusion
As a Major incident, categorised as a restrictive practice
As a Low incident for information only
It is not recorded on DATIX, only in the Electronic Patient Record
rationale: The LTS record keeping section states the practice must be recorded via DATIX as Major and as a Restrictive Practice. This is a step up from the Moderate DATIX required at the start of a seclusion episode.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: A patient in seclusion at the Radbourne Unit needs intramuscular lorazepam.
question: How does the June 2025 Trust procedure say this is managed?
options: It is kept in the ambient cupboard in the seclusion suite with the other emergency medication
It is collected from the on-site pharmacy by the bleep holder
Because it needs refrigeration, it is prepared on the patient's ward and transported to the seclusion suite in a green EVO bag provided by Pharmacy
It is not permitted in seclusion, so an oral alternative must be used
rationale: The June 2025 procedure explains that intramuscular lorazepam needs refrigeration, so it is prepared on the patient's ward and transported to the seclusion suite in a green EVO bag provided by Pharmacy. Other stock injectables and emergency medicines sit in an ambient cupboard in the seclusion suite accessed by a key safe.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: For a second time, the team judge it is not safe to enter the seclusion room to carry out a review.
question: What does Trust policy require next?
options: Escalate to the bleep holder, who determines the further escalation route such as the Area Service Manager or on-call manager, and consider completing a DATIX
Skip the review and record it as not required
End the seclusion immediately
Wait until the next scheduled review and try again
rationale: The policy says reviews should be carried out in the seclusion room where safe and therapeutic, and if it is deemed not safe to enter on more than one occasion the team must escalate to the bleep holder, who determines the further escalation route, with a DATIX also to be considered.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: The team are considering tear-proof clothing for a patient in seclusion with a very high risk of using shredded clothing to self-harm.
question: What does the Trust policy require before this is used, and where is it recorded?
options: The nurse in charge can decide, recorded in the case notes
An individualised Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) risk assessment, with the use recorded in the 'Seclusion Support Plan'
Approval from the Head of Nursing, recorded on DATIX
It is a standard precaution for all patients in seclusion so no separate assessment is needed
rationale: The policy requires an individualised risk assessment by the MDT before tear-proof clothing is used, records that use in the 'Seclusion Support Plan', and states it must never be a first line response, never substitute for enhanced observation, and never be a blanket rule within a service.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)

scenario: The first 24 hour Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) review has taken place and seclusion is continuing.
question: What is the medical review requirement from that point onwards under Trust policy?
options: Medical reviews continue every four hours
Medical reviews are only required if the nursing team request one
Medical reviews must take place at least twice in every 24 hours
Medical reviews reduce to once every 24 hours alongside the MDT review
rationale: The policy states medical reviews must take place at least twice every 24 hours after the initial MDT review, while nursing reviews stay two hourly and MDT reviews continue at least once every 24 hours.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Seclusion and Long-Term Segregation, Psychiatric Emergency Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: Nov 2024, issue 9, review Nov 2027 (version control amended 18 Apr 2026)
